english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies after 30th January 2024 due to changes made by the Online Safety Act 2023. For the offence of sending a false communication under the Online Safety Act 2023 applying after this date, see H101561.
(ii) Consider section 1(1) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 which covers offences in relation to sending of indecent, offensive or threatening letters, electronic communications or articles with intent to cause the recipient distress or anxiety. Although, note, offences H12181 and H12180 under section 1 of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 are also repealed by the Online Safety Act 2023. Consider also an offence under the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(iii) The Penalty Notice for Disorder was raised from £80 to £90 as from 1/07/13.
(iv) As of 13th April 2015, the time limit on prosecution for offences under section 127 of the Communications Act 2003 has been amended. An information or complaint must be laid before the end of the period of 3 years beginning with the day on which the offence was committed, and before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which evidence comes to the knowledge of the prosecutor which the prosecutor considers sufficient to justify proceedings.
(v) The amendment to the time limit (outlined in note (iv) above) applies only in relation to an offence committed on or after 13th April 2015 - for offences committed prior to this date the time limit on prosecution is 6 months from the date of commission of the offence.

As from 08/04/2013 Penalty Notices for Disorder may only be issued to offenders aged 18 years or over.

This offence may be disposed of by the issue of a Penalty Notice for Disorder - PND Code DA02

Penalty Notice for Disorder - Ninety pounds.

Note:

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Complex - see section 127(5)
